items.title: UnitedHealth Stock Recovered Before Its Margins Did
items.summary: UnitedHealth (UNH) stock has gained about 41% since early March, and at roughly $400 a share the market has already paid for a recovery. The easy reading is that the turnaround is finished. It is not. One half got better over those six months, the other got worse, and the price reflects the good half.

items.title: CVS Stock Has Left Its Peers Behind. Or Has It?
items.summary: The market has crowned this healthcare giant the winner of its group, but a look at the underlying business raises the question of whether the celebration started too soon.

items.title: The Bull Case For Cigna Group (CI) Could Change Following Its New Connected Benefits Platform Launch
items.summary: Cigna Healthcare recently introduced an industry-first connected benefits experience that links medical and supplemental health coverage to simplify access to cash benefits for unexpected health events, with Medical with Smart Coverage slated to begin offering supplemental cash of up to US$7,000 per covered event from January 2027 for eligible mid-sized employer plans. items.title: 2 of Wall Street’s Favorite Stocks Worth Investigating and 1 We Turn Down
items.summary: Wall Street is overwhelmingly bullish on the stocks in this article, with price targets suggesting significant upside potential. However, it’s worth remembering that analysts rarely issue sell ratings, partly because their firms often seek other business from the same companies they cover.

items.title: Market Shocks Are Not Where Hims & Hers Health Stock Has Fallen Furthest
items.summary: Its deepest fall inside a market shock is not its deepest fall, and that gap is what a holder should size for.

items.title: UNH Stock Gets Cheaper Only If The Margins Come Back
items.summary: Consensus knocks a quarter off the health insurer's earnings multiple over two years, part of it measurement, and almost none of it from selling more coverage.

items.title: Is CVS Stock Set for a Rebound?
items.summary: Its market-shock drawdowns have been ordinary in depth, and some of its longest waits back to the old high came after falls the index barely noticed.
